xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4645: Anywhere foundation: machine keys, secure channel, machine tokens, owner column and machine links

plan.title: Anywhere foundation: machine keys, secure channel, machine tokens, owner column and machine links
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The Anywhere epic (pan-2350 rev 5) already decomposed the work into about 25 issues and assigned W-SEC1, W-SEC4, W-SEC5, W-CONV1 and W-LINK1-3 to this foundation issue, which #4650, #4651, #2356, #4652, #4404, #4654 and #4656 each depend on. The secure channel, the machine credential and the link store are mutually dependent (a link is useless without the channel and the credential), so the plan stays one issue and is decomposed into 22 serialized-where-needed items instead.

narratives.Problem: Overdeck machines cannot reach each other securely. There is no machine key, no encrypted channel, no machine-scoped credential, no record of which machine owns a conversation, and no way to link two machines and keep a connection to the best route. Every other Anywhere issue is blocked on these pieces. Separately, require_token_mint defaults to off, so a reverse proxy lets remote visitors mint a root session, and plain-HTTP LAN browsers can receive session cookies.
narratives.Proposal: Give each machine an X25519 key; carry all machine-to-machine HTTP and WebSocket traffic inside Noise IK channels (XXpsk0 with the pairing code for pairing) using noise-handshake and secret-stream, over raw TCP on the dashboard port or WSS through Tailscale Serve; add a machine token kind bound to the peer key with D-9 scopes, a restricted /ws/rpc and 4401 revocation; add conversations.environment_id/released_to with backfill; add machine links (pan machines link|list|unlink, Settings Machines panel, Link both ways, machine-links.json), advertised and learned routes, and a link supervisor with heartbeat and freeze-vs-network diagnosis; turn require_token_mint on automatically and refuse plain-HTTP remote browsers. Full detail in .pan/drafts/PAN-4645.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No overdeck.ai directory, direct or relay routes (#2356); no SSH machines (#4404); no Fly machines (#4652); no pan connect (#4656); no fleet versions or Update all (#4654).
- No changes to pan pair on npx machines (#4628) or Traefik binding (#4299).
- No Set up Tailscale flow (#1254); only read tailscale status --json when the binary exists.
- No linked-conversation cache, merged list, remote control, Pull here, released_to writers or title-bar states (#4650, #4646).
- No fencing of agent mutations to link-started conversations, no load in the heartbeat, no --machine flag (#4651).
- No route-scope rows for routes that do not exist yet (worker spawn, release/transfer/settle, costs and settings reads).
- No stream multiplexer, no ENVIRONMENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump, no dedicated link port unless the D-4645-4 checkpoint falls back.
- No per-conversation privacy flag and no machine-key rotation.
- Must not raise any scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt cap; conversations.ts, ws-rpc.ts, settings-api.ts and cli/index.ts must not grow.
- Must not let any machine credential satisfy admin, and must not treat a channel request as a loopback or trusted local caller.

autoDecisions.summary: noise-handshake@4.2.0 + @hyperswarm/secret-stream@6.9.2 are the vetted Noise library (W-SEC1 checkpoint); XXpsk0 is supported natively so the pairing code is the PSK
autoDecisions.rationale: Live probe on 2026-11-01 proved XXpsk0, IK, impostor refusal and HTTP/WS over secret-stream with ciphertext on the wire; the only alternatives (libp2p-noise XX-only, noise-c.wasm 2022) lack IK or are stale.

autoDecisions.summary: One Noise session per transport connection; no stream multiplexer
autoDecisions.rationale: No vetted multiplexer fits; IK is one round trip and HTTP keep-alive pools amortise it; every route kind opens extra connections cheaply.

autoDecisions.summary: Raw TCP channels share the dashboard port through a first-byte (0x00) dispatcher, with a dedicated port 3017 as the implementation-checkpoint fallback
autoDecisions.rationale: D-2 requires raw TCP on lan/tailnet and the W-SEC1 check forbids plaintext HTTP on the wire, which rules out a plain WebSocket upgrade; the sniff probe showed HTTP keeps working.

autoDecisions.summary: Reconnect back-off caps at 45 s for network failures (300 s only for identity-refused routes)
autoDecisions.rationale: W-LINK3 requires online within 60 s of plugging back, which a 300 s cap cannot meet; the operator-facing contract wins over the generic FR-3 number.

autoDecisions.summary: require_token_mint YAML can only add: false cannot switch it off while remote access exists
autoDecisions.rationale: The lossy whole-document Settings save writes the read value back, so honouring an explicit false would freeze the insecure state after a link appears.

autoDecisions.summary: The Use HTTPS refusal is always on for remote plain-HTTP browsers, independent of require_token_mint
autoDecisions.rationale: A session cookie over plain LAN HTTP was never safe; the W-SEC4 done-when names the page unconditionally.

autoDecisions.summary: ENVIRONMENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 1; link compatibility uses the new machineLinks capability and linkProtocol field
autoDecisions.rationale: Bumping the protocol would make existing desktop-app clients see every server as incompatible.

autoDecisions.summary: /ws/rpc scoping uses a restricted PanRpcGroup chosen at upgrade
autoDecisions.rationale: RPC middleware sees per-message headers, not the upgrade credential, so per-method checks cannot see the credential.

autoDecisions.summary: Machine tokens stay in access-tokens.json with kind machine and are bound to the peer machine key
autoDecisions.rationale: D-9 names a new token kind; binding to the key means a stolen token is useless without the machine key.

autoDecisions.summary: Owner column backfill runs at every primary boot (fills NULLs only); vault rows fill from the browse manifest on the next refresh
autoDecisions.rationale: ensureEnvironmentIdentity is async and cannot run in the sync schema top-up; the manifest is the only local source of the owner id.

autoDecisions.summary: WI-8 moves archived listing out of conversations.ts before W-CONV1
autoDecisions.rationale: conversations.ts is above the 1000-line ceiling and may not grow; agents may not raise allowlist caps.

autoDecisions.summary: Link supervisor and channel listener run only on primary dashboards
autoDecisions.rationale: Peer dashboards share OVERDECK_HOME and would hold duplicate channels with the same machine key.

autoDecisions.summary: Live two-machine verification is a script run by the work and test roles, not a CI test
autoDecisions.rationale: Two dashboards need two OVERDECK_HOMEs and a build; module-level singletons prevent an in-process version.

autoDecisions.summary: One plan with sizeJustification instead of more sibling issues
autoDecisions.rationale: The epic already split Anywhere into about 25 issues and names this one as the single dependency of seven siblings; re-splitting would change the operator-authored issue body.

items.title: WI-1 Machine key file, Noise dependencies and descriptor key

expected_outputs: machine-key.test.ts and environment-descriptor-key.test.ts report all tests passed

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. Pin noise-handshake@4.2.0 and @hyperswarm/secret-stream@6.9.2 in dependencies, bun install, add noise-handshake, @hyperswarm/secret-stream, sodium-universal, sodium-native to deps.neverBundle in tsdown.config.ts and src/dashboard/server/tsdown.config.ts (D-4645-2). items.title: Given no machine-key.json, when ensureMachineKey() runs twice concurrently, then exactly one file exists with mode 0600 and both calls return the same 32-byte public key
When machine-key.json holds invalid JSON, ensureMachineKey() throws an error naming the file path and the file contents are preserved unchanged
GET /api/environment returns machineKey decoding to 32 bytes, linkProtocol 1 and capabilities.machineLinks true, while protocolVersion stays 1
machineKeyFingerprint() returns five dash-separated groups of four lowercase hex characters for a fixed test key
WI-2 Secure channel core: wire format, Noise IK/XXpsk0, ChannelSocket, open and accept

metadata.parallelSafeReason: All files are new under src/lib/anywhere/channel/; no existing module is modified.
expected_outputs: channel.test.ts and channel-capture.test.ts report all tests passed

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2 and the Interfaces section; this is the stream interface every downstream Anywhere issue builds on, land it first. Create src/lib/anywhere/channel/{wire,noise,channel-socket,accept,open}.ts exactly per D-4645-1, D-4645-3, D-4645-5, D-4645-17. noise-handshake does the IK and XXpsk0 handshakes with its default X25519 dh; @hyperswarm/secret-stream with the handshake option frames transport bytes; never hand-roll crypto framing. ChannelSocket extends stream.Duplex, remoteAddress = link:<16 hex of remote key>, carries channel marker {mode, remoteKeyHex, pairingId}, counts ciphertext bytes on a copy (secret-stream decrypts in place). open.ts supports tcp://host:port and wss://host/ws/link and maps failures to ChannelOpenError codes; timeouts use AbortController+setTimeout, never AbortSignal.timeout. accept.ts enforces 10 s handshake timeout, 1024-byte frames, isPinnedPeer after IK msg1 (refusal 01), takePairing before XXpsk0 msg1 (refusal 03), link protocol mismatch refusal 02. Tests use real loopback TCP between two in-process endpoints plus a byte-logging TCP proxy.

items.title: Given an IK initiator holding the wrong responder key, when openChannel runs, then it rejects with code identity-refused and the responder HTTP server receives zero requests
Given a byte-logging TCP proxy between initiator and responder, when a GET and a POST run through the channel, then the captured bytes contain neither "HTTP/1.1" nor the POST body text
When XXpsk0 runs with the right pairing code, both sides report the other static key; with a wrong code openChannel rejects with pairing-refused and onPairingFailure is called once
Given an initiator key that isPinnedPeer rejects, acceptChannel sends refusal 01 and openChannel rejects with unknown-peer
When a ws WebSocket upgrades over a ChannelSocket and the server closes with code 4401, then the client receives close code 4401
WI-3 Channel listener on the dashboard port and the channel-peer leaf

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Only server.ts is shared, and every other item touching it is ordered after this one by an edge.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3 and D-4645-4. Create src/dashboard/server/channel-peer.ts (leaf: channelOfIncoming, channelOfRequest via NodeHttpServerRequest.toIncomingMessage, null for non-Node requests) and src/dashboard/server/channel-listener.ts (installChannelListener: swap the http server connection listeners for a first-byte dispatcher; 0x00 => acceptChannel, else unshift and call the saved listeners; /ws/link upgrade via ws WebSocketServer noServer + createWebSocketStream; max 32 pending handshakes => refusal 04; Map of live channel sockets by peer key with closeChannelsForPeer and closeAllChannels; installed only on primary dashboards). Call it from the NodeHttpServer.make factory in server.ts after the setup* calls and close all channels on shutdown. Implementation checkpoint: if the dispatcher breaks existing dashboard tests or the live pan up smoke, fall back to a dedicated listener on anywhere.link_port (default 3017) and record the fallback in continue.json.

items.title: Given the listener is installed on an http.Server, when a client sends a keep-alive pair of GETs, a 200 KB POST and a WebSocket upgrade, then each returns the same response as without the listener
When a socket starts with the 0x00 preamble and completes the IK handshake, a request through it arrives with req.socket.remoteAddress starting "link:" and channelOfIncoming(req) returns the marker
Given 32 handshakes already pending, when a 33rd channel connects, then it receives refusal frame code 04 and is closed
When closeChannelsForPeer(key) is called, every live ChannelSocket for that key closes

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4, D-4645-9, D-4645-10, D-4645-16. access-tokens.ts: scopes gain read:costs, read:settings, forward; kind gains machine with required machineKey (64 hex), environmentId, access; isRecord accepts machine only with all three; MACHINE_TOKEN_SCOPES(access); findActiveMachineTokenByKey; listActiveRecordsOfKind; onAccessTokensRevoked(listener) fired from refresh and revoke for records that became revoked or vanished. New leaf src/lib/anywhere/link-actor.ts (parseLinkActor, effectiveScopes; missing stamp => agent; agent-fenced downgrades operator). dashboard-auth.ts: DashboardCredential machine arm; resolveDashboardCredential(headers, channel) per D-4645-9 (root, device and token credentials resolve to null over a channel); rejectUnauthorizedDashboardRequest passes channelOfRequest. remote-request-gate.ts: pass the channel; channel requests never reach the trusted-local rule; a pairing-mode channel passes the gate for exactly GET /api/environment and POST /api/machines/exchange (before the credential check) and gets 401 elsewhere; a non-channel POST /api/machines/exchange gets 401. ws-auth.ts authorizeDashboardUpgrade gains a channel parameter, and ws-terminal, ws-voice, ws-autopreso, ws-rpc pass it. device-connections revocableCredentialId covers machine.

items.title: Given a machine record bound to key K, when its token arrives over a plain socket or over a channel with another key, then resolveDashboardCredential returns null; over a channel with key K it returns a machine credential with the FR-7 scopes
When the internal token header or the root session cookie arrives over a channel, then resolveDashboardCredential returns null

Given an x-overdeck-link-ceiling header of read:events, when a machine credential resolves, then credentialScopes returns only read:events and never admin; with no actor header the actor resolves to agent

When another process marks a record revoked, the next refresh tick fires onAccessTokensRevoked with that record id (fake timers)

WI-7 /ws/rpc closes with 4401 and cross-process revokes close sockets

metadata.parallelSafeReason: main.ts edits are ordered after WI-9 and before WI-18 by edges; ws-rpc-auth.ts is shared only with WI-6, which precedes it.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7, D-4645-15 and D-4645-16. Implement the 4401 close: find the ws WebSocket on toIncomingMessage(request).socket via Object.getOwnPropertySymbols(socket).find(s => s.description === "websocket") and call close(4401, "device revoked"); never yield request.upgrade twice (upgradeEffect is not cached). If the lookup finds nothing, ship close-without-code and record the deviation in continue.json. Export registerRevocationClosers() from ws-rpc-auth.ts (closeDeviceConnections for every revoked record, closeChannelsForPeer for machine records) and call it in main.ts right after startAccessTokenRefresh().

narrative.Action: PRD WI-21 and D-4645-22. New scripts/anywhere/two-machine-smoke.mjs: requires npm run build; starts two node dist/dashboard/server.js with OVERDECK_HOME=<repo>/.tmp/anywhere-a|b on ports 3041/3042; starts a byte-logging TCP proxy in front of B; pan pair --url http://127.0.0.1:<proxyPort> --json on B and pan machines link <url> --allow-loopback on A so the pairing route and heartbeat cross the proxy; waits for both lists to show the other online (<= 15 s); kills B and asserts offline on A within 30 s; restarts B and asserts online within 60 s; asserts no HTTP/1.1 in the proxy capture; stops both processes; touches nothing outside .tmp/anywhere-*. Not in CI. The work agent runs it before pan done and pastes the output into the PR description.

items.title: When run against a fresh build, the script exits 0 after both dashboards list each other as online within 15 s
When dashboard B is killed, the script observes offline on A within 30 s, and online within 60 s after B restarts
The script fails with exit 1 naming the step when the proxy capture contains "HTTP/1.1"
